title: api-gateway: connector-key principals (verificationLevel 'api_key') fail meetsVerificationLevel against 'none' — every Platform-S originate 403s once the doc-type catalogue is seeded
description:
**BLUF:** `meetsVerificationLevel('api_key', 'none')` **returns false because** `'api_key'` **is not in** `VERIFICATION_LEVEL_ORDER` **(**`indexOf` **→ -1, and** `-1 >= 0` **is false). So once the document-type catalogue is seeded, every** `POST /api/documents` **from a Platform-S connector key is refused with** `INSUFFICIENT_VERIFICATION_LEVEL` **— even though** [KS-388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388/k-freeze-documenttype-as-a-strict-enum-originate-flat-anchor-metadata) **seeded** `SSD_DOCUMENT` **as "deliberately friction-free" with** `creatorVerificationLevel: 'none'`**. Fix is a few lines in** `services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`**; this is the K-side root cause of** [PS-519](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-519/originate-403s-under-connector-keys-k-wants-a-verification-level-api).

## Symptom

Platform-S app log, on every upload under a connector key (135–142 occurrences per full S suite run):

```
CardanoAnchor: originate POST status=403 body={"success":false,"error":{
  "code":"INSUFFICIENT_VERIFICATION_LEVEL",
  "message":"This document type requires NONE verification. Your current level is API_KEY."}}
```

S then falls back to flat `/api/anchors`, which succeeds — so the anchor badge goes green but **no K document exists**: no content-hash resolution for `/api/verification/verify`, no lineage root, no lifecycle events. S's `@k-live` suite fails 11/14 on this alone.

Reproduced 2026-09-16 on Peter's Mac, slot 4 pair: platform-k `0b25f823f` (develop, fresh worktree, fresh volumes) ↔ platform-s `2fa69634` and again `d36ff71e` (develop). Two full S suite runs, 12 failures each, 11 of them this.

## Builds under test

| Platform | Branch | Commit (full SHA) | Slot |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| platform-k | `develop` | `0b25f823f6660ac52b665f14055799ff0c3b616d` | 4 — gateway `:7182`, `secuura_slot4`, fresh worktree + fresh volumes |
| platform-s (run 1) | `develop` | `2fa696340967313fef214bfe1232f17a69cec410` | 4 — `https://localhost:5422`, `ssd-slot4` |
| platform-s (run 2) | `develop` | `d36ff71e5d347089c5cff08a0892bd8cb0e45385` | 4 — same slot, `--rebuild --reset`; `/Health/Data` `build.Commit` matched |

## Cause

`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`

* `:39` `VERIFICATION_LEVEL_ORDER = ['none','basic','social','standard','enhanced','high','government']`
* `:53-57` `meetsVerificationLevel(userLevel, requiredLevel)` = `ORDER.indexOf(user) >= ORDER.indexOf(required)`
* `middleware/auth.ts:276` sets `verificationLevel: 'api_key'` on every connector-key principal.

`'api_key'` is not in the order → `indexOf` = `-1` → `-1 >= 0` is false → a connector key fails even `none`. Any other unknown level string fails the same way.

The check is only reached when `resolveDocumentType` finds the type. On an unseeded K it returns null and `:110-127` (the [KS-388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388/k-freeze-documenttype-as-a-strict-enum-originate-flat-anchor-metadata) fallback) passes through — which is why the failure appears and disappears between rebuilds, and why [PS-519](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-519/originate-403s-under-connector-keys-k-wants-a-verification-level-api) saw the suite "green 2h earlier against the previous K". `routes/admin.ts:283-303` seeds `SSD_DOCUMENT` with `creatorVerificationLevel: 'none'` and says why: *"deliberately friction-free … gating either would break those paths."* The ordering bug defeats that intent. Confirmed on the live K: `GET /api/document-types` lists `SSD_DOCUMENT`, `creatorVerificationLevel: none`.

## Fix (either; the first is narrower)

1. In `meetsVerificationLevel`, an unknown `userLevel` satisfies `requiredLevel === 'none'` only — treat `indexOf === -1` as index 0 when the requirement is `none`, and still refuse any higher requirement, so a connector key cannot originate a `STANDARD`-gated type by accident.
2. Or place `'api_key'` explicitly in the order — but where a machine credential ranks against human KYC levels is a product decision, not a bug fix.

Either way the message should stop rendering `NONE` as harder to meet than `API_KEY`.

## Verification

* Unit: `meetsVerificationLevel('api_key','none') === true`; `meetsVerificationLevel('api_key','standard') === false`; an arbitrary unknown string behaves the same as `'api_key'`.
* Live: S upload under a connector key against a **seeded** K → originate `201`; S `@k-live` `chain_match.spec.ts` green; `POST /api/verification/verify` resolves the document by content hash.

## Related

* [PS-519](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-519/originate-403s-under-connector-keys-k-wants-a-verification-level-api) — the S side (surface K's `error.code` instead of the "revoked or wrongly scoped" guess); its open question "deliberate tightening or seed drift?" is answered here: neither.
* [KS-388](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-388/k-freeze-documenttype-as-a-strict-enum-originate-flat-anchor-metadata) — the catalogue seed that arms the check.

nodes.title: KS-1176: a connector key's verification level ranks as none, so a connector key can create a none-level document type

nodes.body:
**The check this ticket owes: Platform-S uploads under a connector key, on kintsugi, 6 Nov 2026.** dev-ps wrote two uploads, and each confirmed:

* document 24 (`weakestlink-01-hook.png`), K `23417570-3992-4f5a-8894-297485e32653`: tx `fbde1f22cbaa7e36…`, block 4829158.
* document 25 (`test-07-unicode.pdf`), K `d7163cda-a6f8-40cb-bceb-28dc0d325dbb`: tx `1a70dd416c735821…`, block 4829159.

Both were confirmed at 01:29:38 UTC, and on-chain metadata carries each document's own hash and id. S sent `x-api-key`, with the actor unverified.

**Not shown:** I can't see whether kintsugi's document-type catalogue is seeded, which is the condition in this ticket's title. Your side can read that. S's app log for that hour was lost when dev-ps restarted at 02:51 UTC, so the evidence is the ledger and the chain.

**BLUF:** Not run on kintsugi: needs a connector key. Delivered: PR 1014 merged as fa887f382b21 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at ee1e1b832115 (kintsugi's REVISION head, read 2026-11-04 01:59Z). Left open.

- **Owed check:** a Platform-S upload under a connector key.
- **Why not run:** This sweep holds no connector key, and an upload writes a document on a shared box.

**BLUF:** Delivered: PR 1014 merged as fa887f382b21 on develop, deployed to kintsugi at b1fb543640e7 (carried deploy record of 2026-11-01, not re-measured today). Verified by code read, not observed live: `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts:63` ranks an unrecognised verification level as none (`userRank = userIdx === -1 ? 0 : userIdx`), which is how a connector key's api_key level now compares. Left open: observation owed. The merge comment of 2026-09-16 keeps the ticket open until a live Platform-S upload under a connector key is run against a seeded K: live sweep owed (write), not run on kintsugi.

## BLUF

PR #1014 merged. A connector key's `api_key` verification level (any unrecognised level) now ranks as `none`, and the connector document-type allow-list resolves `documentType || type`. **This ticket stays In Progress.**

`Merged fa887f382b212b8da4a0a4a556bacb05ea34daaa; offline gates green; NOT Done per secuura-test-discipline §5f — live sweep owed (torn-down rebuilt stack, all containers verified up), unverified: the live Platform-S upload under a connector key against a seeded K, a real originate, and the production platform-settings shape`

## Recommendation

No action needed now. The live sweep is batched into the Sunday QA pass. Three findings from the round-2 gate are filed as separate Backlog tickets (see Detail); one of them is built next as a follow-up PR.

## Detail

**The merge** (Wednesday's GO 2026-09-16 22:41:29Z, spf/dkim/dmarc pass; tier-1 round-2 delta gate GO WITH FINDINGS at `9ba0caf78b8ddb737541df38303b776c982521d2`, no Blocker; F-1 closed: 0 disallowed types admitted on head and merged, 32 at round 1):

* Squash `fa887f382b212b8da4a0a4a556bacb05ea34daaa` at 22:44:35Z, pinned with `--match-head-commit 9ba0caf78…`.
* Verified at origin: develop tip = the merge commit; one parent = `7e89318bcedbc9a35757d4298ace54a6a23020bd` (#1016); tree `5748a1d68318ed2e310a360fb79e7a1ebc63c785` = the merge-tree prediction; 3 files = the PR's.
* The GO's equality targets hold: `enforcement.ts` `be466fbf4`, `verification.ts` `28fb58343`, `ks1176-connector-key-level-ranks-as-none.test.ts` `43cebf8d7`. The verification.ts blob differs from the PR head's by design: #1016 landed first in the same file, ~900 lines apart.
* Reports: round 1 `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1176-1014-616c766a5-tier1-r1/report.md`; round 2 `…/2026-09-17-ks1176-1014r2-9ba0caf78-tier1-r2/report.md`.

**Records assigned to merge time (fix-round mail, 21:09:01Z):**

* The workflow-bypass connector row.
* `PROPERTY_DEED` ranks at `none`: a product question, not answered here.
* The "nothing beyond anonymous" premise was vacuous, because anonymous is 401 first. Round 2 reworded the why-comment to "an unrecognised level ranks as none, the lowest authenticated level" (R-c, now CLOSED).
* KS-1190 already names `verification.ts:554-557` (the unknown-REQUIRED fail-open, left as it was at base).
* The tenant spoof is stripped by the app chain.
* No level marker is sent on the forward.
* `x-api-key` is not declared on the spec operation.
* Two catalogue sources exist, and the seed is off in production.

**Records from round 2:**

* **R-10:** the allow-list matches exactly, while enforcement matches case-insensitively and by id. That is fail-closed: 23 false refusals on head (e.g. `ssd_document`, `dt-seed-7`), 10 at base; no legitimate shape is newly refused against base.
* **R-g, extended:** `type` is not declared in `DocumentCreateRequest`; the 403 text does not mention the allow-list refusal.
* PR #1016's `ks1072-…test.ts(124,10)` TS18046 shows on develop under a test-including program. It is #1016's record (KS-1180), not this PR's.

**Filed from round 2 (Backlog, not built by this merge):** N-1 (served `data.documentType` unchecked, Major, pre-existing), N-4 (untyped body from a restricted connector stored as DOCUMENT, Minor, pre-existing), and N-2 + N-3 together (a STRING allow-list substring-matches; no both-present precedence cell, Minor). N-2/N-3 is built next as a tier-1 follow-up PR.

## BLUF
PR #1014 round 2 is at head `9ba0caf78b8ddb737541df38303b776c982521d2` and awaits its QA delta gate. The round-1 QA gate found that a connector restricted to certain document types could name any type through the `type` field instead of `documentType`, and this change had widened that. Round 2 fixes it in the same PR: the allow-list now reads the same key enforcement reads.

## Recommendation
No action needed. This ticket stays open: a live sweep is owed after merge.

## Detail
- **Fix:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts`, the connector allow-list resolves `documentType || type`.
- **Measured in-process at the new head:**
  - a connector restricted to `DOCUMENT` naming `SSD_DOCUMENT` via `type` is refused 403 (201 at round 1);
  - the same via `documentType` is refused 403;
  - `DOCUMENT` via `type` still passes;
  - an untyped body behaves as before.
- **Suites:** api-gateway 49 files / 428 tests pass; packages/shared 44 / 851 pass; tsc rc 0. A seven-row tamper table in the PR body reds exactly as predicted.
- **The round-1 gate's other findings are separate tickets, not built:** KS-1195 (per-key rate limiter), KS-1196, KS-1197, KS-1198.

## BLUF
PR #1014 (https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1014) is open for this ticket at head `616c766a57a51238450c99bbf1d59bb109e3841c`, awaiting its tier-1 QA gate.
- **The fix:** in `meetsVerificationLevel` (`services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts:53-64`), an unrecognised user level such as a connector key's `api_key` now ranks as `none`. It satisfies a `none` requirement and nothing higher. This is the narrower of the two fix shapes in this ticket.
- **What it restores:** a connector-key `POST /api/documents` on `SSD_DOCUMENT` passes enforcement. Every type above `none` still refuses a connector key.

## Recommendation
No action needed. This ticket stays open after the merge: the live half of its verification (a Platform-S upload under a connector key against a seeded Platform K, then `POST /api/verification/verify` resolving it) is still owed.

## Detail
- **Measured in-process, at the PR head** (the real router and the real enforcement, with a mocked document-type catalogue):
  - a connector key creating `SSD_DOCUMENT` passes enforcement (403 before the fix);
  - a connector key creating a `standard` type is still refused 403 `INSUFFICIENT_VERIFICATION_LEVEL`;
  - the verifier gate on `POST /api/documents/:id/verify` still refuses a connector key on a standard-gated type.
- **Unit cells:**
  - `api_key` vs `none` → true; `api_key` vs `basic` / `standard` → false;
  - an arbitrary unrecognised string behaves exactly as `api_key`;
  - every known level pair is unchanged (225 rows).
- **Not changed, and filed separately:** an unknown REQUIRED level still passes every authenticated caller. That is KS-1190. The PR pins today's behaviour so it cannot move silently.
- **Not changed:** three other level-order copies with no production callers (auth and shared `requireVerificationLevel`, shared `policy-engine`) and the issuer frontend's upload pre-check. The PR records them.
- **Suites at the head:** api-gateway 49 files / 423 tests pass; packages/shared 44 / 851 pass; tsc rc 0. A six-row tamper table in the PR body reds exactly as predicted.
